items.quote: So let’s go over to the camp of the Arameans and surrender.
items.contrast: The men consider entering the city but reject it as fatal; they instead decide to surrender at the Aramean camp.
items.reason: The quoted sentence directly states their decision after they conclude that remaining where they are will lead to death.

items.quote: The total number of family leaders over the fighting men was 2,600. Under their command was an army of 307,500 men trained for war
items.contrast: The 2,600 family leaders command the army, whereas Jeiel and Maaseiah are involved in mustering and organizing it.
items.reason: “Their” refers to the immediately preceding family leaders, making them the commanders of the 307,500 men.

items.quote: Jeroboam did not change his evil ways
items.contrast: Jeroboam does not change his evil ways, but he does appoint priests again.
items.reason: The reader must preserve the sentence’s negation rather than confuse what Jeroboam fails to do with what he actually does.

items.quote: These four were descendants of Rapha in Gath, and they fell at the hands of David and his men.
items.contrast: Jonathan kills the one huge man described in this episode, while David and his men are collectively credited with defeating all four descendants.
items.reason: The final sentence explicitly assigns the fall of the four to David and his men.

items.quote: he lived there because he was afraid of his brother Abimelek.
items.contrast: Jotham relocates because he fears Abimelek, not because of the citizens of Shechem, whose later hostility is directed against Abimelek.
items.reason: The causal statement uniquely supports the key, but “live elsewhere” is an avoidably vague description of fleeing to and living in Beer.
